newsitem.title: UK: UK chemicals chiefs convicted of "cooking books".
newsitem.headline: UK chemicals chiefs convicted of "cooking books".

text.p: Two former top executives of MTM Plc were convited on Monday of "cooking the books" and misleading investors and analysts about how profitable the fine chemicals company was, the Serious Fraud Office said.

Following a lengthy investigation brought by the SFO and the North Yorkshire police fraud squad after 250 million stg was wiped off MTM's share price in 1992, the former chairman and founder of MTM, Richard Lines, was convicted of two offences of conspiring to account falsley and on one charge of making misleading, false or deceptive statements.

Former finance director Thomas Baxter was also convicted of one false accounting offence and one count of making misleading statements, an SFO statement said. Baxter was cleared on a further charge of conspiring to account falsely.

"Lines and Baxter, assisted by others, cooked the books...in order to give the impression that the company was a good deal more profitable than was, in fact, the case," said Vivian Robinson, prosecuting for the SFO.

In a series of meetings in March 1992, after the company had issued a profits warning, Lines and Baxter continued to "lie to investors and analysts as to the true trading position of the company," the SFO said.
